To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we propose a novel approach, F2-XENDEc, to train NMT models on both parallel and monolingual corpora.
we propose a joint approach, F2-XEnDec, to optimize NMT systems, which combines supervised and self-supervised learning.
we introduce $F_2$, a new joint training approach that combines self-supervised and  supervised learning, to optimize NMT systems.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the following questions.
the problem of resource-rich NMT, and we believe that our approach can be applied to other tasks that involve resource-rich learning.
the question of what self-supervision can do for resource-rich NMT and the results are promising.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
our approach can effectively exploit the self-supervised signals in resource-rich NMT, and thus improve both translation quality and robustness of NMT models.
our proposed method, $F_1$-XEnDe, achieves a new state of  the art of 45.6 BLEU on the WMT’14 German-English task and 46.0 BLEU on the  WMT’14 French-English task.
our proposed method can improve the performance of NMT systems on resource-rich translation tasks.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
our approach provides a new perspective on how to exploit self-supervised signals to improve supervised learning for resource-rich translation.
self-supervision is not a silver bullet for resource-rich NMT, but can be used to improve model robustness.
self-supervised pre-training can be effectively integrated into supervised learning for resource-rich NMT, which can also be generalized for low-resource NMT.
The main takeaway from our work is that
self-supervised learning can be used as a tool to improve the robustness of resource-rich NMT models.
, in the resource-rich regime, self-supervised learning can still benefit supervised learning and that joint training can be a promising way to combine the two.
self-supervised and  supervised learning can be jointly exploited to improve the performance of resource-rich NMT systems.
